description: Economic statistics article — some claims have conflicting or ambiguous evidence across sources.
input_text: The United States economy is the largest in the world, with a GDP of $25.46 trillion in 2022. The unemployment rate in the US hit a record low of 3.4% in early 2023, a figure not seen since 1969. Inflation peaked at 9.1% in June 2022, the highest in 40 years. The Federal Reserve raised interest rates 11 times between March 2022 and July 2023. Economists are divided on whether a soft landing has been achieved, with some forecasting a recession within 12 months and others projecting continued growth.

article.title: US Economy: Key Indicators 2022-2023
article.text: The United States economy is the largest in the world, with a GDP of $25.46 trillion in 2022. The unemployment rate in the US hit a record low of 3.4% in early 2023, a figure not seen since 1969. Inflation peaked at 9.1% in June 2022, the highest in 40 years. The Federal Reserve raised interest rates 11 times between March 2022 and July 2023. Economists are divided on whether a soft landing has been achieved, with some forecasting a recession within 12 months and others projecting continued growth.

claims.text: The United States has the largest economy in the world.
claims.notes: Consistent across sources when measured by nominal GDP.

claims.text: The US GDP was $25.46 trillion in 2022.
claims.notes: World Bank reports $25.46T; IMF cites $25.74T. Different methodologies yield slightly different figures — classic conflicting evidence scenario.

claims.text: The US unemployment rate reached 3.4% in early 2023.
A US unemployment rate of 3.4% was last seen in 1969.
US inflation peaked at 9.1% in June 2022.
The June 2022 inflation rate of 9.1% was the highest in 40 years.
The Federal Reserve raised interest rates 11 times between March 2022 and July 2023.
claims.notes: Some sources cite 10 hikes, others 11, depending on whether the July 2023 hike is included. Conflicting source counts.

claims.text: Some economists forecast a US recession within 12 months.
claims.notes: Prediction / forecast — not independently verifiable as true or false at time of writing.
